name: Usher Syndrome Type II

criteria.description: Moderate to severe congenital sensorineural hearing loss
Later onset of retinitis pigmentosa with progressive vision loss
Normal vestibular function (distinguishing from Type I)
Identification of pathogenic variants in USH2A, GPR98, or DFNB31 genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of moderate to severe congenital sensorineural hearing loss and retinitis pigmentosa with normal vestibular function, supported by genetic testing if available
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Vestibular function testing helps differentiate Type II from Type I Usher syndrome.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Moderate to severe congenital sensorineural hearing loss

pathognomonic.notes: Distinguishes Type II from Type I

occasional.symptomName: Mild balance difficulties under challenging conditions
Delayed diagnosis due to subtle early symptoms

rare.symptomName: Sensorineural hearing loss progression in adulthood

laboratory: Audiometry confirming moderate to severe sensorineural hearing loss
Electroretinography showing reduced rod and cone function
imaging: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing retinal degeneration
Fundus photography revealing bone spicule pigmentation
genetic: Pathogenic variants in USH2A gene (most common)
Variants in GPR98 (VLGR1) or DFNB31 genes
other: Normal vestibular function on caloric and rotational chair testing

distinguishingFeatures: Progressive hearing loss starting in childhood or adolescence
Later onset and variable severity of retinitis pigmentosa

redFlags: Profound congenital deafness (suggests Type I rather than Type II)
references: Smith RJH, et al. Usher Syndrome. GeneReviews. 2020.
Jin H, et al. Usher syndrome type II: clinical and molecular genetics. J Med Genet. 2019.
National Organization for Rare Disorders (NORD). Usher Syndrome Type II. 2021.
